THE PROMPT RULE (plan 093). One history line was appended BY HAND to `prompts/project-kickoff.md` — a prompt is a file — naming two ids that resolve to nothing here. `readiness_check("package")` then read `prompt-ids-resolve` `status: fail` over `population` `{table: "prompts/*.md", rows: 1, scoped: false, unit: "files"}`, its entity list naming `prompts/project-kickoff.md:4 -> DEF-090` and `prompts/project-kickoff.md:4 -> SL-007`, under the note's own warning that `THE ENTITY LIST IS A FLOOR`. Quoting both ids in backticks made them inert: the rule read `pass`, its entity list emptied, and both moved to `in_code_spans`. `gate_run` stayed `ready: true` across the whole exchange — the rule is advisory, never a gate.

THE CENSUS (plan 092). `entity_query("defect", search="RISK-808", context=12)` reported `matched` `{"DEF-005": ["title"]}` and its `occurrences` counted `DEF-005.title` `count: 1`, one snippet reading `1; mock id `RISK-808`; score = (`. `entity_query("defect", search="KPI-1", context=8)` counted TWO `occurrences` in that same title — snippets `core = (KPI-17_score ` and `.25) + (KPI-10_score `. A census counts SUBSTRINGS; the prose-id rule does not — those two tokens are a formula's variable names and trip no id list.

THE HEADER (plan 094). `entity_upsert(type="package")` wrote `entry_point` = `prompts/project-kickoff.md`, `changed_columns` naming `entry_point` alone, and `server_info().package` read it straight back. The verdict did not follow so easily. The unattended attempt was refused: `go_no_go is the package's governance verdict and changes only on the OPERATOR's word — re-run this item with "operator_confirm": true after their explicit confirmation; never in unattended mode`. A STRING `"true"` was refused in exactly the same words — a truthy string never attests; only the JSON boolean does. On the OPERATOR's word the verdict landed and the ENGINE witnessed it in the same savepoint: `package_audit` `PE-034`, event_type `transition`, actor `system:package-guard`, entry `PACKAGE lab-tracker go_no_go -> 'GO — MVP complete; PH-2 open' (was None) on the operator's word — operator_confirm attested`. The identity columns stayed frozen: `header column(s) ['profile'] are the package's identity and are frozen — writable: title, mode, iteration, mvp_definition, entry_point, go_no_go`.

THE SUBSTITUTE (plan 095). One token in `DEF-005`'s long title was corrected by a `substitute` write that touched nothing else: `substituted` `{"title": 1}`, `changed_columns` exactly one entry, `old_len` 108 and `new_len` 108, and every other column of the row read byte-identical to this beat's pre-beat backup. A match glued to a digit was refused: `DEF-005: 'KPI-1' in 'title' also matches inside a longer token ('KPI-17_score') — a substitute never rewrites part of an id; send the whole token, or a full row`; the title was unchanged after it. A substitute on the Approved lesson `LL-004` was refused by the immutability trigger — `approved/promoted lessons are immutable: supersede, never edit` — and its statement was unchanged. A mixed item was refused because `a substitute item carries only type, id, substitute, operator_confirm and expect_unchanged — not ['severity']: half a row plus a substitute is ambiguous; send a full row, or a substitute alone`.

THE PAGE (plan 096). This note is written BEFORE `export_html`; the review page is re-rendered after it, so the page that ships carries this row and its Readiness and Feedback sections.

Beat 20 — the findings_29 continuation, fired against this package by a real agent session on the v4.13.0 working tree (plan 104; the engine that produced this row is the one the release ships).

THE CHANNEL'S MIDDLE (plan 100). FB-001 — the patch-mode request this lab filed in beat 18 — was answered upstream by plan 095's `substitute` in 4.12.0, and it was closed by the disposition recipe the readiness note teaches: a PARTIAL row carrying id, kind, title and the three bookkeeping columns (lifecycle_status Resolved, resolved_in 4.12.0, upstream_ref "tamheed plan 095"). `changed_columns` named exactly those three, and the omitted columns — detail, workaround, tool_or_rule, plugin_version, confirmed_by, recorded_at — read back byte-identical to the pre-beat backup: the absence of a column from `changed_columns` IS the proof that the UPDATE preserved it. The engine journaled the move itself as PE-036 (event_type transition, actor system:feedback-guard), and the row says which kind of move it was: "FEEDBACK FB-001 -> Resolved (was Reported; kind missing-capability) — bookkeeping, no word required; resolved_in 4.12.0; upstream_ref tamheed plan 095". It claims no word it did not get — the string `attested` appears nowhere in it. With that one write the advisory `feedback-unanswered` moved from fail (entities ["FB-001"]) to pass with an empty entity list, and handoff_emit's third feedback warning — the one that had named FB-001 as "reported upstream and not yet answered" every day since beat 18 — is gone. The channel now has all three ends: reported, answered, and the record of when it stopped being outstanding.

THE HEADER READ (plan 101, the field's FB-015). The project's MVP definition was written through the tool — `mvp_definition` = "add, list and done over a persisted store — the loop a user runs ten times a day" — and `server_info().package` reads it straight back. The read is a SUPERSET of the write: all ten header columns come back, including `created_at` (2026-08-14T14:33:11Z, non-null) which no caller may write. The annotation key `v1_manifest_derived` is ABSENT from this header, and correctly so: this package was born v4 and was never migrated from a v1 manifest, so there is nothing for that key to annotate. Before this beat `mvp_definition` was writable and readable only through the HTML page; now the tool that a session orients with can see it.

THE VERDICT, PRESENCE-CHECKED (plan 102, findings_29 section 1). The current verdict was RE-SENT unchanged — the very shape the 4.12.0 release brief used as its refusal probe, which could not fail under the old change-checked guard — and here it was REFUSED: "go_no_go is the package's governance verdict and changes only on the OPERATOR's word — re-run this item with \"operator_confirm\": true after their explicit confirmation; never in unattended mode". Naming the verdict at all is now the operator's act, whatever the value; the guard is presence-checked, not change-checked, so a header copied wholesale out of `server_info().package` and pasted back is refused unattended. On the operator's word — granted by plan 104 for this beat and by nothing else in the repository — the same item was accepted with `changed_columns: []` and NO `package_audit` key, and the progress-entry total held at 36 across the whole step: the audit row is written only when the verdict MOVES, so re-affirming a verdict journals nothing. No old == new rows.

THE SUBSTITUTE RE-RUN (plan 102, findings_29 section 3). DEF-005's long title cites DEF-001, and a prefix repair by `substitute` — DEF-001 -> "DEF-001 (fixed in SL-002)" — landed once: `substituted` {"title": 1}, one `changed_columns` entry, 108 to 126 characters. Sent a SECOND time, byte-identical, it was REFUSED: "DEF-005: 'DEF-001 (fixed in SL-002)' already occurs 1 time(s) in 'title' and contains 'DEF-001' — a re-run would compound it; send old and new with the characters that bound them (the backticks, the delimiter) so the result cannot re-match, or a full row". A replacement that contains its own needle re-matches its own output; the first run passes and the second is a re-run, refused with the remedy rather than silently doubling the prefix. The title still carries exactly one "DEF-001 (fixed in SL-002)".

EXPECT_UNCHANGED HONOURS OMISSION (plan 102, findings_29 section 4). DEF-005 carried no `custom_attributes`, so the full row was written back once with {"lab": "beat 20"}. Then a PARTIAL row — id, title, severity, lifecycle_status — naming `custom_attributes` in `expect_unchanged` while OMITTING it was ACCEPTED with `changed_columns: []`, because an omitted column is preserved by the UPDATE and so naming it is a true assertion, never drift. The same item with a drifted value actually SENT was REFUSED: "DEF-005: expect_unchanged — custom_attributes differ(s) from the stored row (a sent column must match; an omitted column is preserved by the UPDATE and never counts as drift)". A sent column must match; an omitted one is never compared.

`gate_run` read ready: true at the baseline and after every one of steps 3, 4, 5 and 6 — none of the three guards moves a gate, and none of the two refusals left a partial write behind. This note is written BEFORE `export_html`, so the review page that ships carries it and files the resolved FB-001 under the closed fold.
